content.body:
The Châtellerault, as the Mle 24/29 was commonly named, was a design based on the venerable Browning Automatic Rifle (BAR) from WWI. This weapon was commonly found in service with infantry and armored units and, with a larger magazine, was used extensively along the Maginot Line and in fixed defensive positions.
It was durable and hard-hitting, making it popular with the frontline troops.
